sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Linked lists test your ability to manipulate pointers — the fundamental skill in low-level data structure reasoning. Stack and queue problems test your understanding of LIFO/FIFO ordering. Together, these structures underpin browser history, call stacks, task queues, and undo functionality in every application.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
- **Linked List node**: `class Node { int val; Node next; }` — each node points to the next; last node's next is null.
- **Fast/Slow pointers**: Fast moves 2 steps, slow moves 1. When fast reaches end, slow is at the middle. If they meet, there's a cycle.
- **Reversal**: Keep `prev`, `curr`, `next`. At each step: save next, point curr to prev, advance both.
- **Stack (LIFO)**: Push and pop from the same end. Use ArrayDeque in Java.
- **Queue (FIFO)**: Enqueue at rear, dequeue from front. Use LinkedList or ArrayDeque.
- **Dummy node trick**: Create a dummy head to simplify edge cases (empty list, single element) in reversal and merge operations.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
- **singly-linked-list**: Know how to insert/delete/search by traversal; O(n) for all operations.
- **cycle-detection**: Floyd's tortoise and hare — fast/slow pointer. If they meet, cycle exists.
- **reversal**: Iterative reversal with prev/curr pointers is O(n) time O(1) space — must be able to code this from memory.
- **stack-applications**: Valid parentheses (use stack, match opening/closing), min-stack (use auxiliary stack tracking min).
- **queue-deque**: Sliding window maximum uses a Deque (monotonic deque) — add to back, remove expired from front.
- **merge**: Merge two sorted linked lists with a dummy head to avoid special-casing the first element.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- *"How do you detect a cycle in a linked list?"* — Floyd's algorithm: fast/slow pointers meet inside the cycle.
- *"Reverse a linked list."* — Iterative: prev=null, curr=head, while(curr) { next=curr.next; curr.next=prev; prev=curr; curr=next; } return prev.
- *"How do you find the middle of a linked list?"* — Fast/slow pointers: when fast reaches end, slow is at middle.
- *"How would you implement a stack that also returns the minimum in O(1)?"* — Use an auxiliary stack that tracks the current minimum.
- *"Valid parentheses."* — Push opening brackets, pop and match when closing bracket is encountered.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"For this linked list problem, I'll use the [fast/slow pointer / dummy head / prev-curr reversal] technique because [reasoning], which gives O(n) time and O(1) space."*
